title: Open problem: What is the round-trip failure rate decode(encode(d)) != d of shipped, revision-pinned mul
statement: What is the round-trip failure rate decode(encode(d)) != d of shipped, revision-pinned multilingual tokenizer configurations over a dated real-world document corpus, reported per script and per orthographic feature, and does it confound published per-language loss? Posed in print as a metric and never evaluated: the computable part is running TokEval's §3.4 Reconstruction Exact Match and CER over a document corpus on at least 6 shipped configs pinned by revision, with the per-script strata TokEval does not take (it stratifies by byte width) and the meaning-changing split it does not define. VERIFICATION NARROWED THIS ROW AND STRENGTHENED IT. Strengthened: TokEval's Tables 2 and 3 were read in full and Reconstruction Exact Match and CER are ABSENT from their 14 and 9 intrinsic metrics - a NOT FOUND in those words, so the paper names the metric and then does not report it among its intrinsic results. Narrowed: the unreadable-table loss is ONE table, not four, because Appendix A.3 says Table 4 “gives an overview of the panel definitions” and Table 5 “specifies all tokenizers”, which are metadata; only Table 10 could carry a printed value. Also open rather than occupied: per-language BPB is computed over 31 languages UNCONDITIONED on round-trip stability, and no benchmark anywhere is restricted to round-trip-stable text. FLAGGED OPEN-ON-TABLE-10: if Table 10 proves to carry an Exact-match or CER column, this question is ASKED AND ANSWERED for TokEval's 39-tokenizer panel and this row must be WITHDRAWN.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: TokEval, arXiv:2608.18062v3 §3.4 “Encoding Fidelity” and Table 1 (Clara Meister, sole author, from front matter). The load-bearing sentence, reconstructed from three consecutive PDF fragments verified at both junctions and corroborated on the HTML route, is “A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless: the round-trip reconstruction x-hat = T-inverse(T(x)) may differ from the original due to Unicode normalization, UNK substitution, or whitespace handling.” It has no scope-limiting opener, its subject is universally quantified, and it ASSERTS the property; it is also the hedged formulation, the paper nowhere stating a bare “tokenizers are lossy”. §3.4 NAMES AND INTERPRETS the two metrics and defers their definition to Table 1, and it names three mechanisms with “or” rather than enumerating a closed set. No printed value of either metric was reachable at any route across four agents; Table 10 is COULD NOT READ after three renderings, and arxiv.org/pdf/...v3 serves the identical 91,211-character text as the HTML and truncates at the same point, so the one untried route of the right kind is the arXiv e-print LaTeX source, arxiv.org/e-print/2608.18062v3, which carries table bodies as markup no converter can truncate. NEAR NEIGHBOUR TO FENCE OFF: TokEval's printed 0.001 against “0.008 or more” are UTF-8 CHARACTER SPLIT RATES, disjoint from round-trip reconstruction in both directions. Corroborating that the premise is in print and unquantified: TokSuite, arXiv:2512.20757 Appendix A, whose glossary partitions whitespace options into lossy and lossless (“Note that this can result in lossy detokenization”) over 14 shipped tokenizers with no fidelity measurement. CAVEAT ON THE KILL'S REACH, recorded because it bears on how much this row is worth: the second adversary's nine sweeps found no cross-field disguise at all, so the rejection rests wholly on this one definitional prior in a single unvenued preprint with no measurement behind the metric.
inputs.tier: A (limbs a and b: public tokenizer configs plus a public corpus, CPU-only, no training); limb (d) nearer B, since it needs a named published per-language loss gap on a re-runnable eval set and no agent verified one printed
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
